Complete Guide · Module 2

RADAR — Skill Trends

RADAR is a "popularity map": a list of skills widely used by the builder community. The star counts are read directly, honestly, from the GitHub API — not made-up numbers — so you can read which way the wind is blowing and mine ideas for your own skills.

⏱ ≈ 5–6 min read🎯 All beginners📡 Real stars from GitHub API

01 Open RADAR

1

Enter from the Home page

Click the "RADAR — trends" card, or the RADAR tab in the top menu. Every time the tab opens, the app automatically loads the latest data.

What you'll see: a list of skill rows, each with a name, a short description, and a star count (★).

SUCCESS CHECK The list appears with star numbers — that means the GitHub connection is working.

02 Read the list

2

What each row means

Name = the skill's identity. Description = one line about what it does. Stars (★) = how many people starred/liked that skill on GitHub.

How to read it smartly:
  • High stars → well tested by many people; usually tidy and stable format.
  • Low but unique stars → could be a fresh idea few people notice.
  • Notice patterns that repeat across popular skills: those are the proven "standard ways".

Tip: don't just chase the most popular. RADAR is for finding a way of working / a language, not just competing on star counts.

03 Refresh the numbers

3

Press REFRESH

The REFRESH button pulls the latest star counts from GitHub. Useful if the page has been open a while and you want to make sure the numbers are fresh.

Why sometimes needed: popularity changes fast. Refreshing helps you catch shifts before making a decision.

04 Visit the source

4

Click a skill

Clickable rows open the source repo on GitHub in a new tab. There you can inspect the skill content, read its structure, and judge whether the pattern fits your need.

Why useful: the GitHub page shows the original files (e.g. SKILL.md/README), history, and how the author put it together — the most authentic learning source.

SUCCESS CHECK A new tab opens to the matching GitHub repo page.

05 Turn a trend into your skill (the heart of this app)

5

Find → copy the flow → compose your own version

This is RADAR's most valuable part — using it to create work, not just read:

  1. In RADAR, pick a skill that catches your eye, open its repo.
  2. Study its structure & patterns (what parts, what language, what steps).
  3. Open FORGE → in the Telusur GitHub block, search that repo → press Racik to make it a draft.
  4. Turn the draft into your own version better suited to your local need / business.
  5. SAVE.

Tip: the best results come from adapting, not copy-pasting. Create a pattern you like, then adjust the content.

06 Behind the scenes

  • RADAR reads the skill list and requests the latest star counts from the GitHub REST API when the page loads.
  • Clicking an item opens the official repo page on GitHub — not a local copy, so it's always the latest.
  • The Racik button in FORGE uses that repo's identity to pull its files into a draft.

07 Use cases

USE CASE 1 · Find a skill-idea direction

  • Open RADAR, note the highest-starred skills (widely used by teams).
  • Break down their patterns: tidy format, short description, clear steps.
  • Continue to FORGE → search that repo → Racik → adjust to your need.

USE CASE 2 · Research before building

  • You want to make a "how to write a proposal" skill.
  • In RADAR search the booming proposal/template theme, open its repo.
  • See the structure most use → build a version more suited to your local business.

USE CASE 3 · Track what's rising

  • Build a habit: open RADAR weekly, press REFRESH.
  • Jot down skills that grew significantly.
  • Before others do, compose your version for your own need.

08 FAQ

Are the star numbers made up?

No. The numbers are read directly from the GitHub API — real data, not estimates.

Why must clicking an item open a new tab?

So you never lose your place in the app. After researching on GitHub, just return to this tab and keep composing.

How do I make a popular skill my own?

Use Racik in FORGE to pull it into a draft, then rewrite the content to fit your need — adapt, don't copy-paste.

Do high stars always mean it's good for me?

Not necessarily. Stars mean popularity, not a fit with your problem. Take the pattern, adapt the content to your context.

09 Glossary

RADAR — the module that shows popular skills with real GitHub stars.

Stars (★) — markers of popularity / how many starred the repo on GitHub.

Repo — a project / code storage place on GitHub.

REFRESH — the button that re-fetches the latest star counts.

Racik — the action that turns a public repo into a skill draft in FORGE.

Pattern — the standard way seen repeated in good skills: structure, parts, language.
